conviction_note: The stock trades on the FY guide and cRPO, not on the quarter, and has moved a median 14.7% on its last seven prints. Two observability peers that sold off double digits on beat-and-raise prints this month, and a risk-off software tape, hold the lean down. impact_sum (+2.1) and the scaled number (+1.6) agree in sign and size.

findings.finding: Expectations reset: ESTC is -19.9% over 20 days and -11.7% over 5 days into the print, and -5.4% intraday on print day itself ($78.50, from an $83.01 prior close). That leaves it 26% below its $108 high and 29% below the $111 mean analyst target, after a quarter in which every published FY27 metric was raised. The last print bought +19% on a beat and raise from a much less washed-out setup.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two most recent prints that cleared the guide bar were +12.3% (2026-05-28) and +19.3% (2026-08-27). Two prints that disappointed on the outlook were -14.7% (2025-11-20) and -15.4% (2026-02-26) (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The drawdown has visible causes: a sector-wide software sell-off (IGV, AI-disruption fears, the Anthropic IPO draining capital, rate-hike odds) and October supply from a co-founder (see the insider finding). Neither cause is a company-level negative. Had the market priced a fundamental miss, I would expect estimate cuts or target cuts into the print. Instead Citi raised its target to $132 about 2026-11-12, and the mean target is $111.
findings.independence: Price data from stockanalysis.com. Analyst targets from the same page; Citi's raise is independently reported via TheFly. The sector cause is from https://finance.biggo.com/news/e1d8fafb-b4a8-4ba3-95e9-1f8354218b57.

findings.finding: Elastic has raised its FY27 revenue guide twice, each time by more than the quarter's beat: May guide $1.985-2.000B, raised in August to $1.998-2.010B (+$11.5M at the midpoint against a Q1 beat of ~$8M over consensus). The CFO describes the guidance as 'prudent and risk-adjusted' and expects growth to accelerate through the year, with Q4 the fastest. The Street FY figure (~$2.01B) sits at the top of the range, so the bar is a raise to above ~$2.01B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide decides this stock. A raise above the beat with cRPO 21% gave +19.3% (Aug 2026), and the first FY27 guide plus cRPO gave +12.3% (May 2026). A Q4 guide only slightly above Street with a sequential margin dip gave -15.4% (Feb 2026), and a 'cautious' FY26 outlook despite a beat gave -14.7% (Nov 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the Street is already at the top of the range. If the market were confident of a beat-plus raise it would not have taken the stock 20% lower in a month; a stock pricing a raise would sit nearer its $108 post-print high. The risk-adjusted guide habit is public, but the sell-off suggests the market is pricing a stall.
findings.independence: The guide figures are confirmed by the press release (https://www.01net.it/elastic-reports-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-financial-results/). The Street FY figure of ~$2.01B comes from a separate source (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/elastic-aktie-director-verkauft-2-millionen-aktien-analyst-sieht-ki-potenzial). Shares the Q1 call document with the consensus-beat finding below.

findings.finding: Q2 consensus revenue of $486.7M sits inside the company's $486-487M guide, and EPS consensus is about $0.81 against a $0.80-0.82 guide (whisper $0.88). Elastic has beaten EPS consensus in each of the last four quarters and beat revenue consensus by ~1.7% in Q1 ($478M against $470M). A beat of about 1-2% on revenue is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats were sold twice (-14.7% Nov 2025 on a $0.64 vs $0.58 beat; -15.4% Feb 2026 on a $0.73 vs $0.65 beat) when the guide disappointed. The quarter alone does not move the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the beat is the base case. The EW whisper above guidance shows the buy side expects it. Sized near zero.
findings.independence: Benzinga carries the same $486.7M revenue consensus (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ESTC/charts). The Q1 beat is from SiliconANGLE (https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/27/after-posting-a-solid-earnings-beat-elastics-stock-bounces-higher-in-extended-trading/).

findings.finding: Two observability competitors reported the same calendar quarter this month and fell double digits despite beating. Datadog (2026-11-04) posted revenue +35% to $1.20B and raised its FY guide, but fell as much as 14.6% because its Q4 guide implied ~25% growth and its largest customer cut usage. Dynatrace (2026-11-03) beat revenue by 2% but fell 15.6% on flat net new ARR ($70M) with expansions slipping. The tape is selling observability beats that do not show acceleration.
findings.link: Elastic Observability competes directly with Datadog and Dynatrace for log, APM and metrics budgets, and security is a second shared market. Elastic's total revenue is roughly 40% observability plus security by usage (not disclosed exactly), so the link is the same buyer and budget, not shared revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ESTC's own history: sold -15% twice on outlook disappointments despite beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: ESTC fell after both prints. The peer reaction function, though, says a beat-and-raise is not enough in this tape. Elastic's own guide points to acceleration, unlike DDOG's deceleration, which limits how far the read-through transfers.

findings.finding: Hyperscaler infrastructure growth accelerated in the September quarter: AWS +39.3% (sixth straight quarter of acceleration), Azure ~48%, Google Cloud ~103%, and Synergy puts cloud infrastructure spending +55% at $168B. Elastic Cloud runs on and is sold through those three clouds' marketplaces; its annual cloud growth was 27% in Q1, up from 26%.
findings.link: Elastic Cloud is hosted on AWS, Azure and GCP and sold through their marketplaces. Cloud is a large part of subscription revenue (annual cloud growth 27% per the Q1 call), so hyperscaler consumption is the channel. Elastic has not confirmed any Q2 marketplace figure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cloud is not guided and the company stresses quarter-to-quarter consumption variability. No sourced history of the stock reacting to cloud growth alone.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro-to-company proxy and widely known. The hyperscaler acceleration is mostly AI GPU capacity, so transmission to Elastic search and observability consumption is unconfirmed. Sized small.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Elastic's own Q1 commentary on cloud acceleration is at https://www.webull.com/news/15497663695938560.

findings.finding: Software risk-off into the print: IGV fell 3.4% on 2026-11-17, its fifth one-day drop of 3% or more since 2026-10-16. The drivers were AI-disruption fears (new OpenAI models), the Anthropic IPO drawing up to $64B of capital, and a 95% market-implied December rate hike, with the S&P 500 at a five-month low. The tape punishes high-multiple software reactions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not measurable for ESTC specifically. Peers DDOG and DT reacted -14% to -16% on beats this month in the same tape.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced into the 20% drawdown already. It matters for the reaction because it makes the market quick to sell any wobble in the guide. Kept small and negative.
findings.independence: CNBC on the VIX surge (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/17/wall-streets-fear-gauge-is-surging-again-and-this-time-its-not-just-about-ai-jitters.html), a separate source.
